studies.label: TRIZ-C+LLM vs TRIZ-C experiment on three engineering problems (GT, MB, WT)

arms.name: TRIZ-C+LLM
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix with an LLM assistant and a prompt pack covering problem framing, contradiction parameters, inventive principles, solution generation, and a diversity check. Microsoft Copilot with Smart GPT-5 was recommended; other assistants were permitted if reported (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3).

arms.name: TRIZ-C
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix only, with access to triz40.com and instructions not to use any LLM-based AI assistants (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3).

studies.task: Each engineering student individually generated, selected, developed, and documented a concept for a polymer gear testing rig, a bicycle drive mounting bracket, or wind turbine power maximization using the assigned TRIZ method.

ai_tool.name: Microsoft Copilot with the LLM option Smart GPT-5 (recommended); other LLM-based AI assistants were permitted and actual assistant use is not reported
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3, final paragraph. The paper names the recommended model but does not state its release year.

estimates.outcome: Design quality (expert-rated composite), full-sample Method main effect
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Experts holding PhDs in mechanical engineering rated feasibility, fulfillment of technical requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration on a seven-point scale; design quality is the average of these criteria. Two experts independently rated GT and MB solutions, with their ratings averaged per criterion; another independent expert rated WT solutions. Each student contributed one final solution. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.2.2 continuation. Blinding and inter-rater agreement are not reported.

estimates.notes: This is the full-sample Method main effect from the two-way Problem by Method ANOVA. The Table 2 Total rows are unadjusted descriptive summaries pooling different proportions of the problem groups; they are not printed as adjusted arm levels for this Method test. Following the screening correction, these summaries are preserved in the count quotation but are not entered as this test’s means or SDs or as a separate effect-size record. The paper prints no adjusted arm means, signed Method difference, SE, CI, or standardized effect. The F test alone does not identify direction. The counts were rechecked in the nonparenthesized Table 2 entries: n_treatment = 63, n_control = 51, n_total = 114. The smaller parenthesized counts belong to the self-report survey. The agreed fields were independently checked: question = with_ai and outcome_with_ai = true because LLM assistance was available during production of the scored solution (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3). construct = usefulness because this is a design-quality composite of feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration, not a separately reported novelty score (PDF pp. 4–5, printed pp. 510–511, Section 3.2.2). higher_is = more_creative denotes better design quality in the codebook’s usefulness construct. unit = participant and se_basis = participant because each student supplied one final solution, with expert scores averaged before the ANOVA; n_units remains null because n_total already counts the people. within_person = null because each student solved one problem under one assigned method (PDF p. 4, printed p. 510, Section 3.2.1). The common practice task was explicitly excluded from analysis. The outcome is immediate; no delayed unassisted output was assessed. comparison_type = ai_vs_active because the TRIZ-C control received the non-AI TRIZ contradiction-matrix aid through triz40.com; both arms using TRIZ does not make the control unassisted (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3; creativity-codebook.md, Section 5). The authors flag unequal variances and potentially liberal F tests (PDF p. 6, printed p. 512, Section 4.2). Design quality addresses RQ1 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 508); no preregistration is stated. No numerical effect, count, or uncertainty has been derived.

open_items: The full-sample ANOVA Method effect lacks printed adjusted arm means, a signed difference, a compatible standardizer, an SE, a confidence interval, or a standardized effect. The Table 2 Total means and SDs are not printed as the arm levels corresponding to this model contrast. The unmatched fields remain null; nothing was derived from the F statistic. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512), Section 4.2 and Table 2.

The total randomized count and the arm assignment or timing of the excluded GT student are not reported. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Table 1 note. Analysis counts come directly from Table 2, not degrees of freedom.

The assistants actually used by students and their release years are not reported. Copilot with Smart GPT-5 was recommended but alternatives were permitted. ai_tool.year remains null. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3.

Study countries and the randomization procedure are not stated. The numbered locations in Figure 2 do not identify countries, and author affiliations are not treated as study locations. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Section 3.2.1 and Figure 2.
Separate statistics for innovativeness or the other design-quality components, rater blinding, and inter-rater agreement are not reported. PDF pp. 4–5 (printed pp. 510–511), Section 3.2.2.

The screening form leaves partitioning of the problem groups into samples open. This extraction retains its S1 definition and the joint full-sample Method test. Treating problem groups as separate studies would require reconsidering the WT result; GT and MB do not individually meet the codebook sample-size threshold.
Data and materials are available only from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; no public data or supplement link is printed. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 515), Data availability.
notes: Reconciliation date: 2026-10-10; reviewer/extractor: reconciled. Read both extraction rules and the codebook, the candidate and retrieval records, the citation record, the reconciled screening form including final.open_items, both raw extractions, and the comparison file. Read all 334 lines of the markdown conversion, including the final references, and extracted and read the text of all 10 PDF pages. There is no appendix or supplement in this PDF. All retained numeric values were checked on PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512). The Table 2 text was also checked with pymupdf find_tables using text strategies; the ordinary page text preserves the full parenthesized counts. Figure 4 was viewed through an in-memory PDF render to confirm its self-report outcome labels; no values were read from its bars. The PDF text layer encodes the printed plus sign in TRIZ-C+LLM as U+0001; quotations render it as +, confirmed by the arm names in Figure 2 and Figure 4. Quotation whitespace is collapsed; numeric text and precision are preserved. Both substantive study-field differences in the supplied diff are resolved below. The two extractor slugs describe the same Method main-effect record; A’s slug is retained. There were no estimates unique to either extraction and no additional eligible full-sample contrasts were found. The sole screened outcome S1-O1 is represented by its full-sample Method test; its three screened problem-specific contrasts are individually listed in not_extracted under rule 5. S1 remains the jointly analyzed experiment used by the screening form; numbered student groups were not treated as randomized clusters. lab_rct follows the common test protocol, although GT and MB were course tasks (PDF pp. 4–5, printed pp. 510–511). The assignment-time counts remain null because Table 1 gives an exclusion without identifying its arm or timing. The study and arm analyzed counts, all required agreed estimate classifications, and the F test were independently rechecked. The form reports no shared sample; shared_sample remains null. Country and actual model use are not inferred from affiliations or the recommended assistant. Problem difficulty, prompting experience, and student background cannot be separated (PDF p. 8, printed p. 514). No across-people diversity or after-AI output outcome is reported; the prompt-pack diversity check is an instruction, not a scored outcome. No screening arithmetic or unverified candidate lead was copied as data. No values were computed, and only the designated reconciled JSON file was written.

fixes.quote: The students using TRIZ-C were given access to the https://www.triz40.com/ site and were asked to not use any LLM-based AI assistants.
fixes.basis: Confirmed the verifier flag against the PDF procedure and codebook Section 5. The control was supplied a non-AI problem-solving aid, the TRIZ contradiction matrix through triz40.com. Section 5 defines ai_vs_active as AI assistance versus another aid, and ai_vs_bau as AI assistance versus no assistance. Sharing the TRIZ framework does not remove the explicit aid supplied to the control. This is a codebook classification, not a code printed by the authors. The corresponding sentence in the estimate notes was updated to this rationale; all other note text is unchanged.

kept.why_the_flag_is_wrong: The mechanical quotation flag is caused by the PDF text layer encoding the plus sign in TRIZ-C+LLM as U+0001. After replacing only U+0001 with + and collapsing whitespace, the entire recorded quotation matches the Total block of Table 2 exactly. Figure 2 on PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510) also prints the arm label TRIZ-C+LLM with an ordinary plus sign in extracted text. The quoted numbers are unchanged and directly support 63 treatment participants, 51 control participants, and 114 total for design quality. The parenthesized 62 and 113 are student-satisfaction counts, as the table caption states. No numerical or quotation correction is needed.
